questions.question_text:
A printing press bought for $\$54\,000$ is depreciated by the straight-line method at $\$6200$ per year.
What is its salvage value after $5$ years?

options.why: Gave the total depreciation $6200 \times 5$ instead of the value left.
Subtracted only one year of depreciation instead of five.
Used $n = 4$ instead of $n = 5$ in $S = V_{0} - Dn$.

questions.question_text:
A machine costing $\$19\,500$ is written down to a salvage value of $\$4500$ over $6$ years using the straight-line method.
What is the annual depreciation amount?

options.why: Divided the purchase price by $6$ and ignored the salvage value.
Added the salvage value to the purchase price instead of subtracting it.
Divided the salvage value by $6$ instead of dividing the value lost.

questions.question_text:
A van bought for $\$43\,000$ depreciates by $\$4300$ each year using the straight-line method.
After how many years is it worth $\$17\,200$?

options.why: Divided the purchase price by $D$, which gives the time to reach zero, not $\$17\,200$.
Divided the salvage value $\$17\,200$ by $\$4300$ instead of dividing the value lost.
Added the purchase price and the salvage value before dividing by $D$.

questions.question_text:
An oven costing $\$11\,400$ depreciates by $\$1275$ each year using the straight-line method.
What is the total depreciation after $4$ years?

options.why: Gave the value remaining, $V_{0} - Dn$, instead of the total depreciation.
Gave one year's depreciation rather than the total over $4$ years.
Multiplied $D$ by $3$ years instead of $4$.

questions.question_text:
An asset loses $\$3250$ of its value each year by the straight-line method and is worth $\$14\,750$ after $5$ years.
What was its purchase price?

options.why: Gave the total depreciation $3250 \times 5$ instead of the purchase price.
Added only one year of depreciation to the salvage value.
Added the total depreciation twice to the salvage value.

questions.question_text:
Equipment costing $\$64\,000$ is depreciated by the straight-line method at $9\%$ of its purchase price each year.
What is its value after $7$ years?

options.why: Gave the total depreciation instead of the value that is left.
Used declining balance, $64\,000(0.91)^{7}$, instead of a fixed dollar amount each year.
Subtracted only one year's depreciation of $\$5760$.
Read the last year drawn on the graph instead of extending the line to the horizontal axis.
Used an annual amount of $\$4000$ rather than the $\$5000$ the graph shows.
Extended the line by only one further year, reaching $\$5000$ rather than $\$0$.

questions.solution_text:
The line starts at $\$40\,000$ and falls to $\$10\,000$ after $6$ years.
$D = \dfrac{40\,000 - 10\,000}{6}$
$= \$5000$ per year
$n = \dfrac{V_{0}}{D}$
$= \dfrac{40\,000}{5000}$
$= 8$ years

questions.question_text:
A machine cost $\$45\,000$ and depreciates by $\$2700$ each year using the straight-line method.
What percentage of its purchase price has it lost after $6$ years?

options.why: Gave the percentage of the purchase price still remaining, not the percentage lost.
Gave one year's depreciation as a percentage rather than six years' worth.
Used $5$ years of depreciation instead of $6$.

questions.question_text:
A boat cost $\$88\,000$.
It is depreciated by $\$9500$ per year for the first $4$ years, after which the annual depreciation amount changes to $\$6000$.
What is its value $10$ years after purchase?

options.why: Applied the second amount for only $4$ more years instead of the remaining $6$.
Applied the two depreciation amounts in the wrong order.
Stopped after the first stage and gave the value at the end of year $4$.
